title: With `-x`, progress lines and cursor codes land in the alignments on stdout
body:
`-x` sends alignments to stdout in place of the tabular results. `nail search` also prints its progress lines, such as `indexing query database...`, to stdout with `println!`. It rewrites them with raw `ESC[A` cursor codes, and prints the `results written to` line and the `-s` stats there too (nail/src/search.rs, nail/src/util.rs). The first lines of `nail search -x ... > out.txt` hold that text and the escape codes. A survey of `dev` on 2026-11-02 ran this against the release binary.

## Proposal

Progress lines, status lines and stats go to stderr. nail writes the cursor codes only when stderr is a terminal.

## Cost

A script that reads the progress lines from stdout loses them. The output change needs a changelog entry.
